newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Vietnam to boost sugar output for local demand.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam to boost sugar output for local demand.

text.p: Vietnam's ambitious plan to produce one million tonnes of sugar by the year 2000 to meet domestic demand is taking shape, but many obstacles remain, an industry official said on Thursday.

"We strongly believe the programme has economic and social significance and with the strong support of the government will get good success," Vietnam's Ha Duc Ho, deputy director of the Department of Agro-Forestry Products, said.
He was speaking at an international sugar conference on the Indonesian tourist island of Bali.
No comparative sugar production figures were immediately available.
Ho said that since the launch of the programme in 1995, it had received strong support from sugarcane farmers, state-owned companies and foreign investors.
But some of the problems encountered in implementing the production programme included a shortage of capital and a lack of skilled labour.
Ho said land area under sugarcane cultivation had increased to 240,000 hectares (593,000 acres) currently from 147,800 hectares (365,000 acres) at the end of 1994, and that yields had also increased.
He said that by the 1999, Vietnam will have a total of 41 sugar mills compared to the existing 14.
Vietnam imported an average 50,000 tonnes of sugar a year between 1985 and 1990, while imports averaged 60,000 tonnes a year between 1991 and 1994, Ho said.
He said average per capita sugar consumption averaged just six to seven kg and was expected to increase to 12-13 kg by the year 2000.
The programme would create employment opportunities for some 500,000 people, Ho said.
